analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only (docs/developer/test.md head 558-576, docs/provider/direct-mode.md head 179-213, docs/provider/hardware-requirements.md head 12-15 plus a date bump). No executable source, auth, crypto, or config changed.

direct-mode.md documents an optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP owner hook. It is described as default-absent, with no production callsite and no new advertised model. When installed it reuses the existing local auth, body limits, and cancellation scope. The doc claims inline-image decoding (PNG/JPEG selected by content), a concurrency 429, and rejection of image input while MTP is on. It states cancellation must retain media/KV ownership until native terminal retirement.

The hook's source file (provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Server/NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP.swift) was not supplied. These claims are unverified here: that it sits behind LocalAuthResponder, that image parsing and decoding are bounded, and that media is not written to temp files (cf. T-050). If the hook source lands in the same or a later PR, review it against TB-003, TB-007, T-050 and T-028 (residual KV/GPU data) and the existing local-endpoint auth stack. The documented 429 and concurrency limit matter for T-010 and T-029 (DoS).

hardware-requirements.md states that Super VL has no qualified RAM tier, which is a conservative claim. test.md adds the harness and golden-fixture guidance. No threat-model assumption is invalidated by this PR. There is no change to T-041 or the cache.
